races.name: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Arouet
runners_data.note: Twomey-trained 4yo with a recent course win over 18f on Good, solid similar-going record (2W5P in 7 runs); naturally a prominent racer but the crowded pace map means it may be shuffled toward the rear, which represents a departure from its best position — factor that into win expectations.|

runners_data.name: Mento
runners_data.note: Won last time over 19f on Good but has only three hurdle starts; a genuine front-runner by nature, Cooper's charge is likely to find itself racing in midfield as Mino Des Mottes and others crowd it out, blunting its chance in a shape that rewards track position.|

runners_data.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter under Jack Kennedy for Gordon Elliott; won last time over 17f on Good and has strong form at similar trips, with a tongue-tie and excellent strike-rate of jumping clean — the fulcrum around which this entire race is built.|

runners_data.name: Carmel's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Won a Galway 19f novice hurdle on Good last time for Mark Fahey; a natural front-runner with headgear (hood and tongue-tie) that could make it combative for position, though the crowded pace scenario means it may struggle to fulfil that role — recent fitness and a 7lb claimer (O'Connor) are worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Dawn Coming
runners_data.note: Back after just 11 days for C Byrnes, giving it a freshness edge; 0W4P in similar going conditions tells its own story — consistent but not a winner — and although naturally prominent, the overcrowded pace map is likely to push it back from its preferred spot.|

runners_data.name: Like An Ocean
runners_data.note: Won on debut over hurdles at 16f on Good under Harry Sexton (7lb claimer) for Adrian Sexton; entirely unexposed but that single win is its only evidence and the trainer's 14-day strike-rate (0/4) is not encouraging — maps naturally to prominent.|

runners_data.name: Munsif
runners_data.note: Well-travelled 4yo for C Byrnes with multiple placed efforts at similar trips and going; consistently finishes in the frame without winning (3W from 12 similar-going runs) — prominent type likely to find a position but may lack the finishing kick to trouble the best here.|

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Flagged as a finisher who fades late, with poor recent form (7, R) over shorter trips and a 14/15 record in similar going — a hold-up type genuinely toward the rear, but the stamina concern and absence of meaningful novice hurdle form make this a very difficult winning profile.|

runners_data.name: Witches Familiar
runners_data.note: Mullins/Townend combination on a horse that won its only hurdle start at 16f on Good; the powerhouse booking is the headline angle and, as a natural prominent type, Townend can be trusted to secure an ideal position just off the leader — the pair's 14-day W/R (4/20) underlines live claims.|

runners_data.name: Tex Amare
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and twice placed without winning at similar trips on Good and Soft; style unknown — carries a warning for inexperience — and Danny Mullins adds interest, but two thirds without a win is modest evidence at this level.|

runners_data.name: The Chancie Grey
runners_data.note: Twice placed (5th, 6th) from two hurdle starts and both on Good ground at similar trips; style unknown, trainer strike-rate is 0/23 over 14 days, and there is no meaningful evidence to suggest this horse can compete with the classier entries here.|

races.paceDynamic: Mino Des Mottes is the confirmed front-runner and, with Jack Kennedy aboard for Gordon Elliott, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over 2m½f on Good to Yielding ground at Galway. The problem is that this field is saturated with prominent-minded horses — Carmel's Phoenix, Dawn Coming, Mento, Arouet, Like An Ocean, Munsif and Witches Familiar all want to race prominently — meaning several will be crowded out of their natural position and forced to settle further back than ideal. Mino Des Mottes is therefore unlikely to face serious front-running pressure and should get a soft lead, setting a rhythm that gradually tests stamina without burning off rivals early. This shape strongly favours horses who can track the leader in a genuine prominent position — particularly those with the class and tactical versatility to sit just off the pace and pounce — rather than true hold-up types who will be too far back in a muddling gallop to land a blow. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their position; of those displaced, Carmel's Phoenix (class, trip form) and Dawn Coming (recent race fitness, experience over course and distance) are best-placed to push forward if they choose, but Mino Des Mottes and one or two others are most likely to actually lock up the prominent berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mino Des Mottes Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mino Des Mottes is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and set a measured pace that suits a galloping novice.
scenarios.body: Mino Des Mottes dictates every stride from the front, and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and staying power from the first flight; horses tucked in second or third, able to attack at the last, are ideally positioned. Prominent types who manage to hold a tracking position — rather than those shuffled back — will be the primary threats at the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sustainable enough that a horse sitting second or third can produce a clean jump at the last and score on superior ability.
scenarios.body: With Mino Des Mottes setting an honest but unspectacular gallop, a classier rival who has been travelling comfortably just off the shoulder can exploit a single moment of brilliance at the final hurdle. Witches Familiar (Mullins/Townend) and Arouet (Twomey, recent winner) have the profile to benefit if they secure that tracking position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and several prominent types battle for position, creating a messy contest that sees the leader tire.
scenarios.body: A scrappy, slowly-run affair where the compressed field encounters interference and rivals shuffle wide burns stamina unexpectedly late; horses with the freshness or fitness to sustain a run from the home turn — like Dawn Coming (11 days since last run) or Munsif — could pick up the pieces. This scenario is less likely because Mino Des Mottes is a confirmed front-runner unlikely to be stopped going forward.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring hold-up types into play from deep, despite the field being light on genuine closers.
scenarios.body: William F Browne and Tex Amare are the only truly rearward-positioned runners, but both carry significant doubts — William F Browne has a stamina flag and poor novice form, while Tex Amare is lightly raced and unproven at this level. This scenario depends on a pace collapse that is unlikely given Mino Des Mottes' front-running tendencies, making it a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Witches Familiar and Mino Des Mottes — if Townend slots Witches Familiar directly onto the leader's heels from the outset, it becomes the primary danger the moment Mino Des Mottes meets any resistance at the final flight.

Carmel's Phoenix and Dawn Coming — both are natural front-runners likely to be denied their position; watch for signs of restlessness or crowding in the early stages that could cost them race fitness or rhythm.

Arouet — its redistribution to a rear position runs against its best form profile; if it is forced to track from behind, Twomey's runner may never get into a race where the pace is not strong enough to bring it off the bridle at the right time.

William F Browne — flagged with a fade-in-finish concern and 5 days since last run; watch for it to drop away from the home turn if the tempo is at all honest, which could cause interference in the chasing pack.

Like An Ocean and Witches Familiar — both have only one hurdle run each; jumping accuracy at Galway's testing fences under a competitive field should be monitored, as any hesitation could compromise their prominent positions instantly.

races.name: EASYFIX Iggy Daly Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Can Happen
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won over course and distance on Good last time (25 days ago, fresh enough); proven Galway handler but carries 167lbs and was pulled up twice this season before that win, making reliability the key question.|

runners_data.name: Drombane
runners_data.note: Travels prominently for Willie Mullins and Danny Mullins, runner-up on soft and good ground; 58-day break could mean he needs the run, but the stable's 4/20 recent strike rate keeps him honest.|

runners_data.name: Let's Go La Fichad
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who landed a handicap on Good ground 48 days ago; Ricky Doyle rides and the extra distance of 2m½f suits the way he stays on; needs a clear run from the back.|

runners_data.name: Allo Al Khawaneej
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for C Byrnes, ridden by a 7lb claimer; best run at 20f on Good ground gives him a stamina edge but his sim-going record over this trip (10th/13th) is uninspiring.|

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: Won over course-comparable Good ground and wears no headgear, but the ⚠ fade flag is a live concern in a staying handicap; his sim-going mark at this trip is a single 14th and he tends to go well before weakening.|

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type — five seconds or thirds in his last six — ridden by a 5lb claimer for T Hogan; ran just 23 days ago and his proximity figures on Good ground suit this shape ideally.|

runners_data.name: Timurshah
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on Good ground and a genuine hold-up style; with Conor Smithers up and sim-going form flat, his chance depends on getting a clear run late but the distance of 2m½f is longer than his recent winning trips.|

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse back quickly (11 days) with tongue tie and blinkers; course-and-distance third last time is encouraging but the tight turnaround and sim-going figure of 9/9 suggest he rarely improves on form.|

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Consistent fifth-placer whose five sim-going runs produced five finishes between 5th and 13th — a horse that competes but rarely wins; genuine hold-up style needs a fast enough pace to close into.|

runners_data.name: Westoftignes
runners_data.note: Won on Soft over 2m, placed on Heavy — the Good to Yielding may actually be drier than ideal; came off a 132-day break for Gavin Cromwell and Keith Donoghue, prominent style suits the map shape if fresh enough.|

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott, who is firing 5/40 recently; goes prominently, has four runner-up finishes on Good ground and handles this distance — the booking is the standout angle.|

runners_data.name: Quint Major
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type whose sim-going record (14/15) is grim; rarely threatens at the business end of these handicaps and the big field will make finding a run even harder.|

runners_data.name: Sestini
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, young at four, ridden by a 5lb claimer — uncontested lead is his great advantage; has not yet won a hurdle race (best finish third) but gets to dictate every yard of this 2m½f.|

runners_data.name: Woodstream Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent veteran with blinkers, placed in a 2m4f hurdle on Good recently; nine-year-old carrying 161lbs who has plenty of course experience but consistency in sprint finishes has been an issue.|

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for J J Slevin who has been mapped to midfield due to the volume of back-of-field types in this field; his SOF winning form is over a shorter 14f and the style displacement tempers his finishing-kick potential.|

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Star
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose four recent placings have all come on Good or Soft; because so many horses want the same rear ground, he is likely to find himself in the middle of the pack rather than his natural position off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Mart Lane
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer for Barry Connell who has been pushed into midfield on the map by the sheer volume of front-seeking types; 112-day absence is a concern and his soft-ground form record is the strongest part of his profile.|

runners_data.name: Soldante
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won on Soft for a trainer in solid form (2/10); handles Good to Yielding well and six-length winning margin last time suggests he stays the trip — 5lb claimer Eoghan Finegan claims back some weight.|

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's charge ran just six days ago — the quick turnaround is the primary concern; prominent style suits the map but two refused/unseated runs in recent form (R, U) raise jumping reliability questions.|

runners_data.name: Searcog
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent type who has only run at up to 16f and whose sim-going record (12/15) is poor; Patrick Magee runner back in 10 days suggests the trainer is happy but the step to 2m½f looks a stretch.|

runners_data.name: Figero
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins runner who won over 2m on Good at Tipperary recently (7 days ago, very fresh); his true running style is hold-up but he ends up mapping to midfield here — the quick return after a win is the headline fact.|

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: Won a 2m4f handicap hurdle on Good ground and that stamina profile fits; a natural hold-up horse who will be squeezed further forward than ideal by the size of the field, and tongue tie plus breast plate suggest he needs specific conditions.|

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Placed twice recently in midfield/hold-up style for Andrew McNamara; versatile enough to handle Good to Yielding but, like several others, is a genuine closer who will not get a truly unobstructed position off the pace in a 23-runner race.|

races.paceDynamic: Sestini is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-horse field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — he can slot out and set a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 2m½f without being hassled. The field is heavily loaded with prominent types (Can Happen, Drombane, Hopeful Hero, Westoftignes, Dairy Force, Whats New, Searcog, Soldante) who will mass behind him in the early stages, compressing the race into a convoy-style shape where positions are hard to establish. Several hold-up horses — Desert Friend, Inchiquin Star, Figero, Brosna Town, Metamorpheus — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the sheer number of genuine hold-up types exceeds the space the rear naturally offers in a field this size, meaning their true finishing kicks may be muted by traffic and the inability to find daylight late. The field holds more prominent-hungry runners than can all secure a handy position: Whats New, Hopeful Hero, Can Happen and Dairy Force are most likely to actually push through to prominent ground, with others forced wider or further back than ideal. A sustainable, uncontested tempo from Sestini on terrain that rewards galloping horses means this race shape most strongly favours prominent runners who can travel fluidly just off the pace and produce a sustained, rather than a sharp, finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sestini Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sestini sets an honest but uncontested gallop and prominent stalkers track him into the straight without interference.
scenarios.body: Sestini controls fractions from the front while the field strings out behind; handy, fluent travellers who can sustain their effort up the Galway hill get first run on those deeper in the pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Convoy Congestion, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent mass stalls entering the straight and creates a traffic-choked finish that rewards a powerful, wide finisher from midfield.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of prominent runners means the straight becomes a wall of horses, briefly checking those on the inner; runners who find a clear run wide or emerge from midfield late can reel in the tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sestini Outstays All, Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If Sestini's gallop is slow enough to conserve his stamina reserves and the field fails to organise a coordinated challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: The tempo never truly tests him; rivals who pushed up behind are left flat-footed when he kicks at the second-last and the back-markers lack the positional advantage to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field and leave a clear lane up the outside in the final 2f for a genuine closer.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because so many natural hold-up horses have been pushed into midfield by field size, blunting their capacity to produce a clean late run from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Sestini's early-race jumping — if he flukes a mistake or gets crowded in the first-hurdle rush of a 23-runner field, his uncontested lead advantage disappears and the entire pace scenario resets.|

Whats How (Whats New) ran only 6 days ago and has unseated and refused in recent outings — a jumping error from a prominent position in a tightly-packed field could cause significant interference for those tracking behind.|

The volume of prominent types (Can Happen, Hopeful Hero, Dairy Force, Whats New, Searcog) means early position battles down the back are likely; watch for horses getting checked or forced wide before they settle, particularly in the first mile.|

Dairy Force: the Jack Kennedy booking for Gordon Elliott in a big Galway handicap warrants marking — the jockey/trainer combination regularly targets these competitive staying hurdles and the horse's recent runner-up form fits the race shape.|

Westoftignes returns from 132 days off under Keith Donoghue for Gavin Cromwell — a combination with a habit of landing big-field handicaps fresh, making the layoff less of a concern than it would be with a lesser stable.|

races.name: Eventus Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden

runners_data.name: City Of Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Aidan O'Brien with Wayne Lordan aboard; ran fifth on debut over 6f in similar going 19 days ago and steps up to 7f, which should suit a horse who needs a strong pace to finish — that may not materialise here with Trean likely to control.

runners_data.name: Dakota Jack
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for Paul Flynn on this prominent-travelling colt who ran fifth over 8f last time; drops back to 7f on Good to Yielding and has the profile to sit handy behind Trean and challenge in the straight.

runners_data.name: Hmas Perth
runners_data.note: Debut runner from the Aidan O'Brien yard with a hold-up profile and headgear noted; lightly raced and completely unexposed, making ability assessment difficult, but the trainer's juvenile strike rate at this level commands respect regardless.

runners_data.name: Moliere
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for David Marnane with an unknown running style; the Marnane yard has a 3/23 14-day record and there is no form to anchor expectations — ground and trip are a complete unknown, so this is strictly speculative without a market signal.

runners_data.name: One Number
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's runner has genuine prominent inclinations shown by his form (203 including a second over 6f in similar going) but is mapped to midfield because Trean, Dakota Jack, and Our Boy Bailey are all ahead of him for early position; Dylan Browne McMonagle rides and the horse does have placed form to recommend him, though racing back from his natural spot weakens his chance.

runners_data.name: Our Boy Bailey
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Harrington-trained colt who ran second over 8f last time; steps back to 7f on similar going and is a prominent type well-positioned in the race shape to benefit from Trean's front-running — the 40-day break is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Trean
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for P Twomey who finished third over 6f last time; steps up in trip to 7f where he should be even more comfortable making the running, and W J Lee's tactical ride will be crucial in judging how much he gives away up front — tagged STYLE_FIT as a natural leader asked to be a pacer rather than a challenger.

runners_data.name: Yellow Sky
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides this J P Murtagh-trained colt who ran fifth on debut over this exact 7f trip on similar going 30 days ago; unknown style aside, the step forward from a debut experience over course and distance is a genuine positive and Murtagh's 0/24 14-day record is the only note of caution.

races.paceDynamic: Trean is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Dakota Jack and Our Boy Bailey as genuine prominent types to challenge for early position, the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching over this 7f on Good to Yielding ground. Trean should slot comfortably into the lead without being seriously hassled, setting an honest but controllable tempo that keeps the race together through the middle stages. One Number, despite being a natural prominent racer, has been redistributed to midfield in the mapping because the prominent slots are already accounted for by Trean, Dakota Jack, and Our Boy Bailey — those three are most likely to actually secure early positions. This race shape — a single front-runner dictating a measured pace — classically favours prominent racers who can travel close to the speed and pounce, rather than hold-up types who need a truly searching gallop to generate the closing sectionals to reel in an uncontested leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trean Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Trean leads uncontested at a measured pace, the race sets up for a horse tracking just off the pace to strike in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Trean dictates from the front on Good to Yielding ground and the moderate gallop means hold-up horses have no real pace to chase; prominent types like Dakota Jack and Our Boy Bailey, travelling smoothly just behind, are ideally placed to challenge and sustain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Trean Bowled Over Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong and Trean ties up in the final furlong, a closer with a strong finishing kick collects.
scenarios.body: City Of Gold, as a hold-up type with a good run in similar going, would be the prime beneficiary of any late collapse in the pace, sweeping past weakened leaders; Yellow Sky, with experience over this exact trip, could also pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced horses — Hmas Perth or Moliere — arrives with a significant market move and an O'Brien or Marnane yard reputation, a debut winner is possible.
scenarios.body: Hmas Perth, trained by Aidan O'Brien with a hold-up profile, could be an unknown quantity capable of sweeping through from the back on debut; Moliere, a Marnane runner with strong flat connections, could exploit inexperience in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners push Trean along harder than expected and the race falls apart in the straight, genuine hold-up horses get a rare chance.
scenarios.body: City Of Gold and One Number — though the latter is a natural prominent type pushed back on the map — would be the notional beneficiaries, but One Number racing out of role makes this a low-confidence shape; City Of Gold is the more credible finisher in this unlikely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Trean's early fractions — if W J Lee is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, a conservative pace could see the leader holding on much longer than his SP suggests, catching hold-up horses cold.

Monitor the market for Hmas Perth and Moliere in the final 30 minutes; any significant move for either debutant would indicate stable confidence and could fundamentally alter the race shape if they attract early market support.

Our Boy Bailey has not run for 40 days — watch the paddock for any signs of freshness or fitness concern, as a prominent-style horse who is ring-rusty could surrender position early and undermine the scenario where he stalks Trean.

One Number's redistribution to midfield is worth watching live — Dylan Browne McMonagle may attempt to push forward from the gate regardless of the mapping, and if he succeeds in grabbing a prominent spot, the crowding among pace runners could force Trean into a faster tempo than expected.

races.name: Connacht Hotel (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Holy See
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for William Durkan with a 1/3 trainer 14-day strike rate; has won over similar distances on Good ground and is the controlling pace influence here — the key question is whether his 54-day break blunts the finishing effort after dictating.

runners_data.name: Yashin
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear, Jessica Bedi yard has gone 0/4 in the past 14 days and Yashin's recent form shows a string of mid-teen finishes in similar company — needs the pace scenario to collapse to get involved.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien prominent racer who was second at 14f on Heathrow and has solid placed form; trips up to 20f suit and a strong pace would allow this horse to arrive on the bridle from close range.

runners_data.name: Lark In The Mornin
runners_data.note: Four wins from five Good-ground runs gives this JP O'Brien runner a compelling going profile, and a natural front-to-prominent style means it is ideally placed to harness Holy See's tempo — the best trainer in this race has multiple strings to his bow.

runners_data.name: Glenroyal
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (headgear: p) for JP O'Brien who won over 10f on Soft and 13f on Good — the step back up to 2m1f is a question mark but trainer form is strong and a late surge scenario would suit.

runners_data.name: Granite Bay
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained prominent type with three wins from five on Good-to-Soft conditions and strong placed form at 11-16f; well-suited by a controlled pace that lets him track and pounce without expending energy early.

runners_data.name: Westminster Moon
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type (headgear: t) who landed a 14f win on Good; a trend of mid-field finishes suggests he needs either a truly strong pace or a collapse in fractions, and Martin's yard has been quiet (0/5 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a fades-in-finish flag and headgear (p) — the fade tendency on Good ground over 20f is a concern here, and JP O'Brien's use of the blinkers does not fully mask an unconvincing recent record.

runners_data.name: Sirius
runners_data.note: Long absence (279 days) for Mullins, but won a 12f race on Heathrow and won a 17f contest on Good — headgear (h) is applied and the stamina profile at 2m1f looks solid if fitness is there after nearly ten months off.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Durkan runner who has finished first, second or second in his last three starts and is now 13 days fresh — prominent style on Good ground with a strong recent upward curve makes this one of the more interesting profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Filey Bay
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old for Emmet Mullins (headgear: ht) with four wins from 15 Good-ground runs and a win at 17f; 288 days since last run is the obvious concern, but natural prominent style and proven stamina keep it relevant if fit.

runners_data.name: Light Up The Dark
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien's 5yo has three wins and a win at 13f on Good — a true prominent racer by nature but the crowded front section means it is unlikely to get its preferred early position, limiting its chance to express that style fully.

runners_data.name: Tyson Fury
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent type with two second-place finishes on Good and Soft at 16-17f but no wins at this level recently — Denis Hogan yard has had 3/26 in 14 days and the age and recent record make this a speculative proposition.

runners_data.name: Smooth Tom
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (headgear: v) for Slattery with a second place at 12f on Heathrow and a third at 19f on Good; 17 days fresh and the stamina profile over 2m1f is untested beyond 19f — best served by a slowly-run affair that turns into a sprint.

runners_data.name: Teed Up
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (headgear: t) with a fades-in-finish flag — Emmet Mullins runner returning after 87 days with a string of double-figure finishes on Good over staying trips; the fade tendency is a serious concern given the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Clear Quartz
runners_data.note: Has won on Soft and been placed on both Good and Soft, and naturally wants to race prominently — in this 23-runner field, the front section cannot accommodate its style, so it will likely be shuffled into a position that blunts its strengths.

runners_data.name: Jabbar
runners_data.note: Gerard O'Leary's 7yo has placed figures of 3 and 4 on Soft and Heathrow over 16f, and instinctively wants to race up with the pace — but with so many prominent types in this field, securing that position will be difficult and its chance is tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Mullins 5yo with headgear (p) who has produced a sequence of sixth-place finishes — a natural front-runner who cannot get to the rail in this field, and consistent placed form is absent which compounds the tactical disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Plontier
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (headgear: tp) for Terence O'Brien with a second at 12f on Good; 20 days fresh and a record that shows placed efforts when dropped back in distance — the 2m1f is at the outer limit of its proven stamina.

runners_data.name: Tounsivator
runners_data.note: Four wins from 15 Good-ground runs and a win at 14f just 19 days ago — naturally wants to race in the first two or three but the number of similar types in this field means it is unlikely to get there; the raw form is strong enough to make it dangerous if the race evolves with fluid early positions.

runners_data.name: Daddy Long Legs
runners_data.note: Mullins 7yo with headgear (p) who has won over 18f on Good and placed at 13-16f — a natural prominent type with a strong record on Good ground, but will be further back than it wants; the form is live if it can find a way through on the home turn.

runners_data.name: Highwind
runners_data.note: Mullins 6yo hold-up type (headgear: p) who has a placed record at 14-18f on Good — consistent without winning and returns 31 days since last run; needs the closers' scenario to fully unfold to get into contention.

runners_data.name: Immutable
runners_data.note: Joseph Murphy's 6yo has been placed at 12f on Soft but has no wins in 15 starts and a string of mid-field finishes — a natural prominent type who will not get its preferred position in this field, and the lack of a win strike rate makes it hard to recommend.

races.paceDynamic: Holy See is the one confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, critically, is unlikely to be seriously contested for the lead — the pace map identifies multiple genuine prominent types (Light Up The Dark, Too Bossy For Us, Jabbar, Clear Quartz, Tounsivator, Daddy Long Legs, Immutable) who cannot all secure their natural position and will be shuffled back into midfield. With Holy See able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good To Yielding ground over 2m1f, the pace is likely to be honest but not frenetic — enough to string the field out without turning it into a sprint finish. The field holds far more front-running and prominent types than can realistically get to the front: Holy See, Granite Bay, Lark In The Mornin and Galileo Dame are most likely to actually press forward, with the redistributed horses — Light Up The Dark, Too Bossy For Us, Jabbar, Clear Quartz, Tounsivator, Daddy Long Legs and Immutable — racing further back than they would choose. This race shape — a lone confirmed leader setting a measured tempo — strongly favours horses who can track prominently in the first two to five lengths of Holy See and produce a sustained gallop home, rather than closers attempting a late sweep from the rear who will rely on the pace being genuinely strong enough to set them up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Holy See Controls, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Holy See is allowed to bowl along at a sustainable clip unchallenged and the race becomes a test of class and stamina from two out.
scenarios.body: Holy See dictates on a loose rein, the field strings out on the Good To Yielding ground, and horses who tracked closely in the first few lengths — Lark In The Mornin, Granite Bay, Galileo Dame — arrive with reserves intact to pounce in the straight. True prominent types who got their position benefit most, while redistributed midfielders cannot produce the quick move required.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Holy See's gentle early fractions create a bunched, falsely-run contest that sets up a race-long sprint from the home turn.
scenarios.body: With little genuine early pace, the field compresses and the contest becomes a flat-out dash up the Galway straight, favouring horses with tactical speed coming from mid-division who can quicken off a slow tempo. Smooth Tom, Plontier and Westminster Moon — genuine hold-up types with finishing gears — are best placed to pounce if the pace is deceptively slow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Scrambles, Fresh Legs Tell
scenarios.trigger: If the volume of horses naturally wanting to race forward creates friction early, burning off several prominent types and leaving the winner to come from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Despite Holy See's lone confirmed lead, six or seven horses will instinctively push to the front section of a 23-runner field, creating an unintended competitive early gallop that softens up the leaders and suits a horse dropping in smoothly from just behind. Eagle Fang and Sirius, both prominent types who race with tactical composure, are positioned to exploit a field that has partially talked itself into a stronger gallop than Holy See intended.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Defies Map
scenarios.trigger: If one of the genuine prominent horses pushed back by the pace map manages to secure a forward enough position despite the crowded front section and runs out a surprise winner.
scenarios.body: In a 23-runner handicap chaos at the break or a slow early pace can allow a sharp-jumping type to stride up and claim a front-rank position, meaning a runner like Tounsivator or Daddy Long Legs — both true prominent types with winning course-and-distance profiles — could still get competitive if the early order is fluid. Their style fit is compromised by the redistribution, making this a lower-probability outcome, but the raw form of both makes it a live danger.

watchPoints.text: Holy See must be tracked from the off — if it is allowed any daylight through the first mile on Good To Yielding ground it could prove extremely difficult to reel in, and the single jockey in the field with the most tactical authority over the pace is Ms K M Ryan aboard the race's only confirmed front-runner.

Monitor the first two furlongs closely for crowding: with Lark In The Mornin, Granite Bay, Galileo Dame, Clear Quartz, Jabbar, Too Bossy For Us, Tounsivator, Daddy Long Legs and Immutable all naturally wanting prominent positions, early interference or a stumble in the pack could end the race for several well-fancied runners before it begins.

Eagle Fang's sharp upward form curve (1-2-2 in last three starts) combined with only 13 days since last run raises the question of whether Durkan is pitching this horse in on a short turnaround because it is peaking — watch for it to travel strongly in the early-to-mid stages.

races.name: Clayton Hotel Galway Handicap

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Won two of last three including over 7f at Salisbury, DBM retains the ride, comfortable on Good ground and well-drawn; natural prominent runner who should land a front-rank pitch and is the most in-form horse in the race.

runners_data.name: Expert Dancer
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner whose role here is pace-setter rather than winner candidate, having been away 38 days; the Good To Yielding suits based on a soft-ground win, but setting a solo lead before being swamped is the realistic risk.

runners_data.name: Motta Alta
runners_data.note: Won last time over this trip on Soft ground for Harrington and Foley, giving it the strongest recent form-and-going combination in the prominent group; the step back from 8f to 7f after a break of 38 days is the only pause for thought.

runners_data.name: Final Boss
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has struggled for consistency, finishing sixth on Good and tenth on Soft in recent runs; blinkers fitted, and Matthew Smith's yard is cold at 0/3 in the 14-day window — needs something to go wrong upfront.

runners_data.name: Nazario
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on a horse that has finished placed twice from seven attempts on similar ground; sits naturally prominent but lacks the recent win form to assert, and the drop from 8f to 6f last time before returning to 7f adds a slight query.

runners_data.name: Caitouna
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on Good ground at the Galway Festival, making course-and-distance form a genuine asset; Carroll stays on board, and a prominent run from a fresh enough gap of 18 days gives it a straightforward profile.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Has two placed efforts in eight career starts but none on Good To Yielding; tends to race prominently and the step back to 7f from softer surfaces is unexplored in recent form — limited reason for confidence.

runners_data.name: Templenoe
runners_data.note: Style is unknown (U), off 107 days — the longest layoff in the field — and has only one run on similar going; Slattery switches from Expert Dancer to this, but the absence and unknown tactical profile are significant unknowns.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on this hold-up type wearing a visor; has placed form on Yielding and over 7f at Dundalk, and a clean run from midfield is essential — if the pace is true enough, the finishing kick becomes relevant.

runners_data.name: Girl Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up style who has placed twice at 7-8f on Good ground; W J Lee provides a useful booking and the form includes a third on Soft, but a genuinely weak pace would hurt its chances of closing from the rear.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 6f on Good ground for McGuinness; a natural front-runner whose form figures include placed efforts, but the crowded prominent group means it is likely to race further back than it wants — the style mismatch is the central concern.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary rides a filly with a win and three places on Good-to-Yielding-type ground at 6-7f; genuine pace-seeking style but mapped to midfield due to overcrowding up front — if she can find cover and switch off, the form entitles her to a share of the finish.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) takes the ride; has one win from 15 Good-ground starts and fades late — a tongue tie is fitted, and the hold-up style in a race unlikely to produce a strong pace is a significant tactical disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Coolshine
runners_data.note: Has not finished better than ninth in four starts, all on Good or Soft ground; flagged as a fader in finishes, and although mapped to midfield from a true hold-up profile, there is no form evidence to suggest relevance here.

runners_data.name: Unfamiliar
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on Good ground on debut for K Smith, but the five subsequent runs have produced four eighths; a natural pace-seeker who will be back further than ideal — the debut win is the only form peg to hang hopes on.

races.paceDynamic: Expert Dancer is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse committed to the lead, will dictate a controlled, rhythm-based gallop on Good To Yielding ground over 7f at Galway — a track that already demands stamina through its undulations. Dancing Saxon, Motta Alta, and Nazario will press for prominent positions just off the pace, creating a competitive early order without anyone likely to blow the race up from behind. The field holds more genuine front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate: Dancing Saxon and Motta Alta are most likely to physically secure the positions immediately behind Expert Dancer, while Coincidental Glory, Dervo Annie, and Unfamiliar — all true prominent racers — will be shuffled back against their natural instincts. This controlled, single-pace shape on soft-leaning ground favours horses who can travel prominently in the first three or four and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than those needing a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Expert Dancer sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the horses immediately behind track it comfortably to the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Expert Dancer's economical front-running allows Dancing Saxon or Motta Alta to sit a length or two off the pace in perfect position, then pick up under minimal interference when the sprint begins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so conservative that Expert Dancer's rhythm is never genuinely challenged and the field fails to close.
scenarios.body: Good To Yielding ground and a lack of pressure means Expert Dancer consumes minimal energy leading, and the prominent horses immediately behind never manufacture the sustained challenge needed to reel it in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens slightly more than expected and the prominent group spends themselves, opening the door for a one-run finisher.
scenarios.body: A horse like Sagasti or Girl Bear, settled in the middle of the field with Colin Keane or W J Lee getting a clean passage wide, delivers a sustained finish while the front rank weakens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Lands
scenarios.trigger: If one of the displaced prominent horses — Dervo Annie or Unfamiliar — secures better early ground than their mapped position suggests and runs to their natural style.
scenarios.body: Racing closer to the pace than the field map implies, a horse like Dervo Annie with recent placed form on similar ground could outrun its position, but the style mismatch and crowded early conditions make this the least likely shape to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Coincidental Glory, Dervo Annie, or Unfamiliar — all natural prominent types — can recover early position at the break, because if any of them successfully land up front, the pace dynamic changes materially and Expert Dancer's control evaporates.

Expert Dancer's 38-day absence combined with a solo lead role on Good To Yielding over 7f creates a stamina question in the final furlong — if it stops quickly, the prominent pair (Dancing Saxon, Motta Alta) inherit the race rather than winning a proper battle.

Templenoe returns from 107 days off with an unknown running style — if Andrew Slattery opts to push it forward aggressively to find a position, it could disrupt the early order and inject unwanted pace into what looks like a controlled race shape.

Sagasti (visor, Colin Keane) and Girl Bear (W J Lee) are the hold-up horses best placed to benefit if the race somehow fractures and the prominent group overcooks it — monitor how much daylight Keane gets on Sagasti turning for home.

Galway 7f on Good To Yielding is notably stamina-testing; horses that have already won or placed at the trip on soft-ground variants (Motta Alta, Expert Dancer, Dervo Annie) carry a genuine going-form edge over those whose best form is on faster surfaces.

races.name: Grá Chocolates Handicap

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on soft and placed over 10f on good, giving him the widest going-and-trip profile in the race; Colin Keane's booking is a significant upgrade and he is proven prominent, but he must survive early jostling to get his position.|

runners_data.name: Confused
runners_data.note: Ran 1-4-4 in his three career starts, all on good or similar ground, and Shane Foley knows how to slot a prominent racer into a traffic-heavy race; the headgear (p) may sharpen his early responses, though three runs is a slim profile for a competitive handicap.|

runners_data.name: Themis
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners a horse who has won his last two starts over exactly this trip on good-to-soft and good ground — the form fits the conditions precisely; a hold-up style means he must avoid the congestion battle and trust his class to bring him with one late run.|

runners_data.name: Sir Benji
runners_data.note: Placed in three of three starts and showed a sharp rise in form when winning over 10f on heavy at the Curragh; Gary Carroll will aim to take a prominent position but, with six rivals sharing that ambition, he may be shuffled back further than ideal.|

runners_data.name: Sharkeyboy
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' runner has been off 56 days — the longest absence in the field — and the headgear (p) worn last time suggests he needed a mental spark; showed a place effort over 8f on good going but this 12½f trip looks untested territory for him.|

runners_data.name: Darius Dark
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins over 12f on good ground make him the most directly course-and-distance-relevant horse in the race; Ben Coen steers a horse whose form map is almost purpose-built for today, though the headgear (p) hints he can be keen and must be placed properly in the prominent cluster.|

runners_data.name: So Must I
runners_data.note: Four consecutive fourths reveal a horse who gets into contention but cannot find the finishing kick to convert; Shay Wallace's 7lb claim helps the weight, but his hold-up style leaves him reliant on the race falling apart late, and on this evidence he tends to be one pace in the stretch.|

runners_data.name: Admiral Will Brown
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the only horse certain to get his preferred position; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is advantageous, the recent win over 10f on good is encouraging, and an uncontested lead on Good To Yielding over 12½f gives him every chance of lasting longer than his OR of 78 might imply.|

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.note: Won his last start over 10f on good and has placed in three of five career runs; Andrew Slattery trains and rides, which means information is tight, but a prominent style and solid recent form make him a consistent threat if he can track the early leaders cleanly.|

runners_data.name: Nod Of Approval
runners_data.note: Finished second over 12f on good earlier in the season but has not recaptured that form, most recently fifth over the same trip on good; Keithen Kennedy's 5lb claim softens the weight, but a hold-up style in a 15-runner field with a congested middle pack is a tall ask.|

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: In good recent form — won over 10f on soft — and is a genuine prominent racer who would naturally be tracking Admiral Will Brown; the map has her displaced to midfield because the prominent positions are already oversubscribed, meaning she may face a rougher passage than her ability deserves.|

runners_data.name: Fits Perfect
runners_data.note: Carries a warning flag for fading in the finish and has been off 93 days — the second-longest break in the field; form reads 9-0 in recent starts and a hold-up style means she is dependent on a strong gallop to bring her into it, which looks unlikely given Admiral Will Brown's likely controlled tempo.|

runners_data.name: Ryefield Dasher
runners_data.note: Owns a profile of modest placings and a single sixth on soft going; a true hold-up racer whose best result came over 8f — shorter than today's 12½f — and Thomas Gibney's yard has had no runners in the past 14 days, adding opacity to her fitness.|

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: Placed twice this season on good ground over 10f and looks like a genuine hold-up horse who would benefit from a true-run race; Wayne Lordan's booking adds a measure of confidence, but finishing second in a maiden leaves him untested at handicap level and the map redistribution reflects that he may not get his preferred position to settle.|

runners_data.name: Solas Na Gealai
runners_data.note: Three starts, all finishing 7th or 8th, offer limited encouragement; a natural closer who has been mapped out of her preferred rear position and represents J S Bolger's stable with a low recent-run profile — insufficient form to seriously threaten here.|

races.paceDynamic: Admiral Will Brown is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only a 3lb claimer aboard, should be allowed to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop on Good To Yielding ground over 1m4½f. Behind him, a cluster of prominent types — Madbadanddangerous, Confused, Sir Benji, Sharkeyboy, Darius Dark and Nermal — will jostle for the positions immediately behind the leader, creating meaningful congestion between the 2f and 3f-out markers as the field rounds the home bend. This prominent scrum risks producing a falsely run race in the early stages before the pace lifts, potentially leaving those tucked just behind the scrimmage in the best position to pounce. The field contains more genuine prominent racers than can all secure their natural position: Admiral Will Brown is certain to lead, with Darius Dark and Madbadanddangerous best-credentialled to lock in the prime seats just behind, while Misty Cove — a true prominent type — has been displaced to midfield on the map because there simply is no room for her. This race shape most favours hold-up and late-prominent runners who can navigate the congestion and arrive with a sustained run from 2f out, particularly those proven on similar ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Admiral Will Brown dictates an honest but uncontested tempo and the prominent cluster burns each other out fighting for position.
scenarios.body: Admiral Will Brown sets an even gallop that suits him but leaves just enough in the tank for late arrivals to reel him in around the 2f pole; horses who settled behind the scrimmage and widened into the straight get first run. Themis and Darius Dark, both proven over this sort of trip on similar ground, are the profiles that benefit most from a race that resets in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion resolves quickly and a small group breaks away cleanly, running the hold-up horses out of the race.
scenarios.body: A settled group of three or four prominent racers tracks the leader at an honest clip and the race never truly falls apart at the back of the field, leaving closers with too much ground to make up in the final two furlongs. Darius Dark, who has won three consecutive races over 12f on Good ground and sits right in that prominent pocket, is the standout beneficiary alongside Madbadanddangerous, who has already won at this trip on soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Admiral Will Brown gets a soft enough lead that his pursuers never seriously close the gap entering the straight.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace rival to push him, Admiral Will Brown could be allowed to bowl along at a deceptively comfortable tempo and simply never be headed, especially if the chasing prominent types are too busy watching each other to make a coordinated challenge. This is a low-probability outcome given the weight of prominent horses likely to apply at least modest pressure from 4f out, but the 3lb claim and a recent course win keep it live.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle turns truly messy and the pace spikes dramatically between 3f and 2f out, leaving the field strung out.
scenarios.body: A scenario dependent on Misty Cove, Ryefield Dasher, Vantage Code or Solas Na Gealai — several of whom are racing out of their natural role on the map — producing a big sweeping run from the rear; because these horses are redistributed and not true hold-up specialists in this race context, the probability is low. So Must I has the most genuine staying form of the rear-division runners and is the most credible beneficiary if the pace truly blows up.

watchPoints.text: Admiral Will Brown must be tracked from the first furlong — if Wesley Joyce is allowed to bowl clear unchallenged, the sustainable gallop he sets could make him very hard to reel in on the run-in, particularly if prominent rivals waste energy fighting each other.

The section between 3f and 2f out is the critical danger zone: six prominent horses fighting for four places behind the leader creates a high probability of crowding, checking and wide detours — Madbadanddangerous, Darius Dark and Nermal are the most exposed to traffic interference here.

Themis for Dylan Browne McMonagle should be monitored leaving the back straight — if he is caught in the prominent scrum rather than settled in his natural hold-up position, his finishing run could be compromised before the race reaches its decisive stage.

Misty Cove's true prominent style means she will be pushing against the map in this race; watch whether Robert Whearty elects to press forward early and, if so, whether that forced move costs her petrol when the finish arrives.

Fits Perfect's 93-day absence combined with her fade-in-finish flag makes her worth monitoring in the final furlong — if she weakens sharply it may create interference for closers attempting to come through on her inside.
